picks.excerpt: Incoming BISG executive director Allison Belan says AI 'was the first thing that came up in virtually every conversation' with members and now tops the standards body's agenda. A second industry-wide AI survey lands in fall 2026, aimed at pushing publishers from debate to concrete implementation.
picks.rationale: The body that writes publishing's metadata and supply-chain standards is putting AI at the top of its agenda — whatever it codifies becomes the disclosure and workflow rules every publisher has to implement.

picks.excerpt: The Korea Publishers Society has extended applications for Asian Publishers Week (Seoul, November 3-6), themed 'Publishing in the Era of AI: Between Crisis and Opportunity.' It is the region's biggest scheduled forum on how AI is reshaping editorial, rights and production practice across Asian markets.
picks.rationale: An open application with a live deadline, hosted in Seoul, on exactly the AI-and-publishing question this section tracks — directly actionable for Korean editors and rights teams.

picks.excerpt: Jason Hamilton walks through his full pipeline for adapting his own novel into an AI-generated film — scripting, character consistency, shot generation and edit — as a marketing and IP-extension play for indie authors. A concrete look at where book craft meets generative video production.
picks.rationale: A step-by-step, reproducible pipeline an indie author can run this week to turn a backlist title into video marketing — the most hands-on item in the pool.

picks.excerpt: Wendy Queen and Jonathan Woahn note the scholarly community has twice built the foundational layer only to watch commercial platforms own what sat on top of it. AI participation in scholarship is the third chance — and the terms have to be set collaboratively before the layer hardens.
picks.rationale: Frames the AI-infrastructure decision scholarly publishers are making right now as an ownership question with a closing window — a strategy argument with a deadline, not a think piece.

picks.excerpt: Pope Leo XIV's May encyclical on artificial intelligence is drawing unusual praise across the book trade for its argument that AI must stay human-centred and be brought under real regulatory oversight. Publishing bodies are now citing it as moral cover in licensing and training-data fights.
picks.rationale: Publishing trade bodies are actively citing the encyclical in licensing and training-data advocacy — it is becoming a rhetorical instrument in negotiations, not just commentary.
